    Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan

       The Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan (Accessible India Campaign), launched on December 3,
        2015, aims to create a barrier-free environment for persons with disabilities (PwDs)
        across India. The campaign focuses on three key areas:

           1. Built Environment Accessibility: Ensuring that public buildings are accessible to
       PwDs.

         2. Transportation Accessibility: Making public transportation systems, including buses,
          trains, and airports, accessible.

         3. Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Accessibility: Enhancing access
         to information through accessible websites and digital platforms.

       The campaign aligns with India's commitments under the United Nations Convention on
        the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD) and is implemented by the
       Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD) under the Ministry
        of Social Justice and Empowerment.

         Built Environment Accessibility:

           Audits Conducted: Accessibility audits were completed for 1,671 government
            buildings across 48 cities.

             Retrofitting Efforts: A fund of ₹562 crore was allocated to retrofit 1,314 buildings.

           Accessible Buildings: Accessibility features were incorporated into 1,748
          government buildings, including 648 State/UT buildings and 1,100 Central
          Government buildings.

        Transportation Accessibility:

            Airports: All 35 international airports and 55 out of 69 domestic airports have
          been equipped with ramps, accessible toilets, helpdesks, and lifts with Braille and
            auditory systems.

           Railway Stations: 709 railway stations have been made fully accessible, while
          4,068 stations are partially accessible.

           Buses: Out of 1,45,747 buses, 8,695 (5.96%) are fully accessible, and 42,348
          (29.05%) are partially accessible.

          Bus Stations: Across 24 States/UTs, 3,120 out of 3,533 bus stations have been
           equipped with accessibility features.

         Digital Accessibility:





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-3)                                                                                      4

Central Government Websites: 95 websites have been made accessible under the
           Content Management Framework by the Ministry of Electronics and Information
           Technology (MeitY).

            State Government Websites: 676 websites have been made accessible, with 476
            of them live.

        Education and Language Accessibility:

            Indian Sign Language Research and Training Centre (ISLRTC): Established in
          September 2015 to promote the use, teaching, and research of Indian Sign
           Language.

            Training Programs: Over 1,013 individuals have been trained in Indian Sign
          Language through diploma and short-term courses offered by ISLRTC.

          Diploma Completion: A total of 183 students have completed the Diploma in Indian
           Sign Language Interpretation (DISLI) course between 2016-17 and 2023.

          Media Accessibility:Accessibility Standards: The Ministry of Information &
           Broadcasting has published Accessibility Standards for TV Viewing for persons with
            hearing impairments.

           Accessible Content: 19 news channels have telecast 2,447 accessible news
             bulletins, and 17 General Entertainment Category (GEC) channels have
           broadcasted 3,686 accessible programmes and movies.

      Sugamya Bharat App:

       Launched on March 2, 2021, the Sugamya Bharat App is a crowdsourcing mobile
         application designed to enhance accessibility in the built environment, transportation
         sector, and ICT ecosystem. The app allows users to report accessibility issues and
        provides features like text-to-speech, font size adjustment, and compatibility with
        Android and iOS accessibility modes.

        Transition to SIPDA:

           Initially planned to conclude by March 2024, the objectives of the Sugamya Bharat
        Abhiyan have been absorbed into the Creation of Barrier-Free Environment Scheme
        under the broader umbrella of the Scheme for Implementation of the Rights of Persons
        with Disabilities Act (SIPDA). This transition emphasizes that accessibility is an ongoing
        endeavor requiring sustained efforts to meet evolving challenges.

      Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana

       The Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY), launched in 2017, is a Central Sector Scheme
          fully funded by the Government of India. It aims to provide free assistive devices to
         senior citizens suffering from age-related disabilities, thereby enhancing their quality of
            life and promoting independent living.

        Objectives:




GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-3)                                                                                           5

To provide aids and assistive living devices to senior citizens belonging to the Below
           Poverty Line (BPL) category who suffer from age-related disabilities such as low
              vision, hearing impairment, loss of teeth, and locomotor disabilities.

       Implementing Agency:

          The scheme is implemented through the Artificial Limbs Manufacturing
           Corporation (ALIMCO), a Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Social
            Justice and Empowerment.

          Eligibility Criteria:

           Age: Senior citizens aged 60 years or above.

          Economic Status:

          1. Belonging to the BPL category, or

          2. Having a monthly income not exceeding ₹15,000.

             Disabilities Covered:

          1. Low vision

          2. Hearing impairment

          3. Loss of teeth

          4. Locomotor disabilities

           Documentation:

          1. Valid Aadhaar card or other government-issued identification.

          2. Income certificate from a competent authority.

          3. Medical certificate from a government medical officer or ALIMCO rehabilitation
            expert confirming the disability.

        Additional Notes:

             Beneficiaries should not have received the same device(s) free of cost from any
           government source in the last three years. However, replacement of faulty/non-
             functional devices may be allowed as an exception.

              In any State/UT, 30% of the beneficiaries shall be women.

          The percentage of SC/ST beneficiaries shall be equal to or more than their
            respective percentage of the population in the district.

       Types of Assistive Devices Provided:

        Generic Devices:

           Walking sticks

          Elbow crutches





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-3)                                                                                         6

Walkers/Crutches

           Tripods/Quadpods

           Hearing aids

           Wheelchairs

               Artificial dentures

           Spectacles

        Special Devices:

           Wheelchairs with commode

             Chair/Stool with commode

             Silicon foam cushions

          Knee braces

            Spinal supports

            Cervical collars

           Lumbosacral belts

            Walkers/Rollators with brakes

           Walking sticks with seat

           Foot care kits (including flexi gel socks, cushion sandals, silicon insoles)

          These devices are provided free of cost to eligible beneficiaries. ALIMCO
           undertakes one-year free maintenance of the aids and devices.

     Swachhta Udyami Yojana

       The Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY), launched in 2014, is a central sector scheme
        under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. It aims to promote cleanliness
       and provide sustainable livelihoods to Safai Karamcharis (cleaners) and liberated manual
        scavengers. The scheme is implemented by the National Safai Karamcharis Finance
       and Development Corporation (NSKFDC).

        Objectives:

            Cleanliness: Enhance sanitation infrastructure by supporting the construction,
            operation, and maintenance of community toilets.

            Livelihood: Provide financial assistance to Safai Karamcharis and liberated manual
           scavengers for income-generating activities related to sanitation.

       Key Components:

           1. Community Toilets (PPP Mode)





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-3)                                                                                                  7

Eligibility: Individual beneficiaries or Self-Help Groups (SHGs).

          Loan Amount: Up to ₹25 lakh.

             Interest Rate: Not more than 4% per annum.

           Rebate of 1% per annum for women beneficiaries.

             Additional rebate of 0.5% for timely repayment.

          Repayment Period: Up to 10 years with a 6-month moratorium.

           Subsidy: Maximum of ₹3.25 lakh.

         2. Sanitation-Related Vehicles:

          Eligibility: Manual scavengers, Safai Karamcharis, Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), SHGs, or
        cooperatives.

         3. Loan Amount:

         Up to ₹15 lakh for individuals.

         Up to ₹50 lakh for SHGs or cooperatives.

             Interest Rate: Not more than 4% per annum.

           Rebate of 1% per annum for women beneficiaries.

             Additional rebate of 0.5% for timely repayment.

          Repayment Period: Up to 10 years with a 6-month moratorium.

           Subsidy: Maximum of ₹3.25 lakh.

         4. Implementation and Application:

       Implementing Agency: NSKFDC, through State Channelising Agencies (SCAs), Regional
         Rural Banks (RRBs), and Nationalised Banks.

     Ambedkar Social Innovation Incubation Mission (ASIIM)

       The Ambedkar Social Innovation & Incubation Mission (ASIIM), launched in 2020, is a
         flagship initiative by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of
          India. Implemented through the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC),
        ASIIM aims to promote innovation and entrepreneurship among Scheduled Caste (SC)
         youth, with a special focus on Divyangs (persons with disabilities), by providing financial
        support and incubation facilities.

        Objectives:

           Encourage SC youth to become entrepreneurs by supporting innovative ideas and
             start-ups.

            Provide financial assistance and incubation support to translate start-up ideas into
           commercial ventures.





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-3)                                                                                          8

Promote socio-economic development through innovation and entrepreneurship.

          Eligibility Criteria:

           SC/Divyang youth meeting any of the following conditions are eligible:

             Identified by Technology Business Incubators (TBIs) promoted by the Department of
           Science & Technology (DST) or other government-supported incubators.

             Identified for incubation by reputed private TBIs.

          Awarded under the Smart India Hackathon or Smart India Hardware Hackathon
           conducted by the Ministry of Education.

            Start-ups nominated and supported by corporates through Corporate Social
             Responsibility (CSR) funds.

         Additionally, applicants must:

          Be Indian citizens and lead founders of the start-up.

           Hold at least 51% shareholding in the company.

          Focus on innovation/improvement of existing products, services, or processes with
             potential for employment generation and wealth creation.

       Funding Support:

           Equity Funding: Up to ₹30 lakhs over a period of 3 years to each selected start-up.

            Further Funding: Successful ventures may qualify for additional funding of up to ₹15
            crore from the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC).

       Implementing Agency:

          The scheme is implemented by IFCI Venture Capital Funds Limited, which manages
            the VCF-SC.

     Deendayal Disabled Rehabilitation Scheme

       The Deendayal Disabled Rehabilitation Scheme (DDRS) is a flagship Central Sector
       Scheme under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India.
       Launched in 2003 and revised in 2022, the scheme aims to create an enabling
        environment for the empowerment of persons with disabilities (PwDs) by providing
         financial assistance to non-governmental organizations (NGOs) for various rehabilitation
         projects.

        Objectives:

           Ensure equal opportunities, equity, social justice, and empowerment of PwDs.

           Encourage voluntary action for effective implementation of the Rights of Persons
            with Disabilities Act, 2016.





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-3)                                                                                         9

Provide financial assistance to NGOs for comprehensive services necessary for the
              rehabilitation of PwDs.

          Eligibility of Organizations:

            Organizations eligible to receive grants under DDRS include:

            Registered societies under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, or any relevant Act
            of the State/Union Territory.

            Trusts registered under the Indian Trust Act, 1882, or any other similar Act in force.

             Not-for-Profit companies registered under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013, or
           any relevant Act in force.

        Grants-in-Aid to Implementing Agencies:

              Eligible Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) are entitled to receive 90% of the
             project cost as grants-in-aid.

          The remaining 10% of the project cost is to be borne by the PIA from its own
            resources.

            For projects located in special areas, 100% of the project cost is provided as
             grants-in-aid.

     Assistance to Disabled Persons for Purchase / Fitting of
     Aids and Appliances (ADIP Scheme)

       The Assistance to Disabled Persons for Purchase/Fitting of Aids and Appliances
        (ADIP) Scheme, launched in 1981 and revised in 2022, aims to assist persons with
          disabilities (PwDs) in procuring durable, modern, and scientifically manufactured aids
       and appliances to promote their physical, social, and psychological rehabilitation.

        Objectives:

            Provide durable, modern, and scientifically manufactured aids and assistive devices
             to PwDs.

           Promote physical, social, and psychological rehabilitation of PwDs.

          Reduce the effects of disabilities and enhance the educational and economic
             potential of PwDs.

          Eligibility Criteria:

            Citizenship: Indian citizen of any age.

              Disability: Holding a 40% Disability Certificate (Benchmark disability) as defined in
            the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016.

       Income:

           Monthly income up to ₹22,500: Eligible for full assistance.




GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-3)                                                                                                          10

Monthly income between ₹22,501 and ₹30,000: Eligible for 50% assistance.

           Dependents: In case of dependents, the income of parents/guardians should not
          exceed ₹30,000 per month.

           Previous Assistance: Should not have received assistance during the last 3 years
              for the same purpose from any source. However, for children below 12 years of age,
            the minimum time of assistance is one year.

      Quantum of Assistance:

           Aids/Appliances costing up to ₹15,000: Full financial assistance is provided.

           Aids/Appliances costing between ₹15,001 and ₹30,000: Assistance up to ₹15,000.

           Aids/Appliances costing above ₹30,001: Government of India shall bear 50% of the
             cost. The remainder shall be contributed by either the State Government, NGO, any
            other agency, or the beneficiary concerned, subject to prior approval of the Ministry
          on a case-to-case basis.

        Special Provisions:

           1. Cochlear Implant:

            For children with pre-lingual hearing loss (1 to 5 years): Up to ₹7.00 lakh per unit.

            For children with acquired hearing loss (5 to 18 years): Up to ₹6.00 lakh per unit.

          The financial support covers the cost of the implant, surgery, therapy, mapping,
              travel, and pre-implant assessment.

         2. Corrective Surgery:

          Speech & Hearing Impaired: Up to ₹1,500.

             Visually Impaired: Up to ₹3,000.

            Orthopedically Impaired: Up to ₹15,000.

       Implementing Agencies:

               Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation of India (ALIMCO).

            National Institutes and Composite Regional Centres under the Ministry of Social
            Justice and Empowerment.

              District Disability Rehabilitation Centres (DDRCs).

            State Corporations in the field of Disability.

            Registered NGOs and Voluntary Organizations.

      Inter Caste Marriage Scheme

       The Dr. Ambedkar Scheme for Social Integration through Inter-Caste Marriages is a
         central government initiative launched in 2013–14 to promote social harmony by




GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-3)                                                                                                                                        11

encouraging inter-caste marriages, particularly between Scheduled Caste (SC)
         individuals and those from non-SC communities. The scheme provides financial
        assistance to eligible couples to support their union and initial settlement.

        Objective:

          To appreciate the socially bold step of an inter-caste marriage taken by newly
         wedded couples and to extend financial incentive to enable them to settle down in
            the initial phase of their married life. This scheme aims to promote social integration
          and reduce caste-based discrimination.

          Eligibility Criteria:

            Inter-Caste Marriage: One spouse must belong to a Scheduled Caste, and the other
             to a non-Scheduled Caste.

              First Marriage: Both spouses should be entering into their first marriage.

           Legal Marriage: The marriage must be valid as per the law and duly registered
           under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

            Application Timeline: The proposal should be submitted within one year of
            marriage.

          Income Limit: The total annual income of the couple should not exceed ₹5 lakh.

           Aadhaar-Linked Joint Bank Account: Couples must have a joint bank account linked
            with Aadhaar numbers.

         No Prior Incentive: If the couple has already received any incentive from the State
          Government/UT Administration for this purpose, the amount approved/released will
          be adjusted from the total incentive under this scheme.

        Incentive Details:

            Total Incentive: ₹2.5 lakh per eligible couple.

          Immediate Release: ₹1.5 lakh is released to the couple's joint account upon
            approval.

           Fixed Deposit: ₹1 lakh is kept in a fixed deposit for three years and released along
            with accrued interest after this period.

            Additional Support: An amount of ₹25,000 per inter-caste marriage is provided to
              District Authorities for organizing a befitting programme in which the incentive is
          handed over to the couple.

    SAGE- Senior Care Aging Growth Engine Initiative

       The Seniorcare Ageing Growth Engine (SAGE) Initiative is a program launched by the
         Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, on June 4, 2021. It





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-3)                                                                                                            12

aims to promote entrepreneurship in the field of elderly care and to provide a platform
         for start-ups offering innovative products and services for senior citizens.

        Objectives:

           Encourage entrepreneurs to develop solutions addressing the needs of India's
           growing elderly population.

              Identify, evaluate, and support start-ups offering products and services in areas
          such as health, housing, care centers, finance, food, wealth management, and legal
            guidance.

              Facilitate access to these solutions for senior citizens through a dedicated portal.

       Funding and Support:

         An allocation of ₹25 crore was made for the SAGE project in the financial year 2021-
            22.

          Each selected start-up is eligible for a one-time equity support of up to ₹1 crore.

         An additional ₹100 crore has been assigned for promoting the silver economy, which
           focuses on the needs and potential of the elderly population.

      SAGE Portal Features:

          The SAGE portal serves as a "one-stop access" point for elderly care products and
            services provided by credible start-ups.

            Start-ups can apply to be part of the SAGE initiative through this dedicated portal.

         An independent screening committee of experts selects start-ups based on the
            innovativeness and relevance of their products and services.

          The Ministry acts as a facilitator, enabling senior citizens to access these products
          and services through the identified start-ups.

     SMILE Scheme

       The SMILE (Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise)
       scheme, launched in 2021-22, is a comprehensive initiative aimed at providing welfare
       measures to the transgender community and individuals engaged in begging.

        With an outlay of ₹365 crore for the period up to 2025-26, the scheme encompasses
       two sub-schemes:

          1. Central Sector Scheme for Comprehensive Rehabilitation for Welfare of
          Transgender Persons

          2. Central Sector Scheme for Comprehensive Rehabilitation of Persons Engaged in
           the Act of Begging

       Sub-Scheme: Welfare of Transgender Persons:





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-3)                                                                                                           13

Key Components:

          1. Educational Support: Scholarships are provided to transgender students from Class
             IX up to post-graduation to encourage continued education.

          2. Skill Development & Livelihood: Under the PM-DAKSH scheme, skill development
             training is offered to enhance employability and livelihood opportunities.

          3. Healthcare Services: In convergence with PM-JAY, the scheme supports gender-
             affirmation surgeries and related medical procedures through selected hospitals.

          4. Shelter Homes – Garima Greh: Establishment of 'Garima Greh' shelter homes
            provides safe housing, food, medical care, and skill development opportunities for
           transgender individuals.

          5. Transgender Protection Cells: Setting up of protection cells in each state to monitor
          and address offences against transgender persons.

          6. National Portal & Helpline: A dedicated portal and helpline have been launched to
            provide information and assistance to the transgender community.

       Sub-Scheme: Rehabilitation of Persons Engaged in Begging:

       Key Components:

          1. Survey and Identification: Conducting surveys to identify individuals engaged in
           begging to facilitate their rehabilitation.

          2. Mobilization: Efforts to motivate and bring individuals into the fold of rehabilitation
             services.

          3. Shelter Homes: Provision of shelter homes that offer food, clothing, medical care,
          and education for children of persons engaged in begging.

          4. Comprehensive Resettlement: Initiatives aimed at providing vocational training, skill
           development, and employment opportunities to ensure sustainable livelihoods.

    PM-DAKSH Scheme

       The Pradhan Mantri Dakshta Aur Kushalta Sampann Hitgrahi (PM-DAKSH) Yojana,
        launched in 2021 by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, aims to enhance
        the employability and livelihood opportunities of marginalized groups through skill
        development.

        Objectives:

            Elevate the skill levels of target youth by providing short-term and long-term
              training, followed by assistance in wage or self-employment.

         Empower marginalized communities, including Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other
          Backward Classes (OBCs), Economically Backward Classes (EBCs), De-Notified,





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-3)                                                                                                         14

Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs), and Safai Karamcharis (including waste
             pickers).

          Eligibility Criteria:

         Age Group: 18–45 years.

        Target Groups:

           SCs.

         OBCs with annual family income below ₹3 lakh.

         EBCs with annual family income below ₹1 lakh.

          DNTs.

             Safai Karamcharis (including waste pickers) and their dependents.

        Training Components:

           1. Upskilling/Reskilling:

          Focus on rural artisans, domestic workers, sanitation workers, etc., in their existing
            vocations.

            Includes financial and digital literacy.

            Duration: 32 to 80 hours over up to one month.

            Stipend: ₹2,500 per trainee towards compensation of wage loss.

         2. Short-Term Training:

            Various job roles as per National Skill Qualification Framework (NSQF)/National
           Occupational Standards (NOS).

          Focus on wage/self-employment opportunities.

            Duration: 200 to 600 hours, up to 6 months.

            Stipend:

           ₹1,500/month for SCs and Safai Karamcharis.

           ₹1,000/month for OBCs, EBCs, and DNTs.

         3. Entrepreneurship Development Program (EDP):

            For SC and OBC youth with an entrepreneurial bent of mind.

            Includes sessions on business opportunity guidance, market survey, working capital
          management, business plan preparation, etc.

            Duration: 80–90 hours (10–15 days).

         4. Long-Term Training:

             Training in sectors with high demand in the job market for wage-placement.





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-3)                                                                                                            15

Programs as per NSQF, NCVT, AICTE, MSME, etc., in areas like production
            technology, plastic processing, apparel technology, healthcare, etc.

            Duration: 5 months to 1 year (up to 1,000 hours).

            Stipend:

           ₹1,500/month for SCs and Safai Karamcharis.

           ₹1,000/month for OBCs, EBCs, and DNTs.

         Financial Assistance:

            Training Cost: 100% grants by the Government.

            Stipend:

           Short-Term and Long-Term Training:

           ₹1,500/month for SCs and Safai Karamcharis.

           ₹1,000/month for OBCs, EBCs, and DNTs.

              Upskilling/Reskilling:

           ₹2,500 per trainee towards compensation of wage loss.

           Attendance Requirement: Minimum 80% attendance to be eligible for stipend.

        Implementation:

           Implementation Period: 2021–22 to 2025–26.

    Scheme for Economic Empowerment of DNTs

       The Scheme for Economic Empowerment of De-notified, Nomadic, and Semi-
       Nomadic Tribes (SEED) is a flagship initiative launched by the Ministry of Social Justice
       and Empowerment on February 16, 2022. It aims to empower historically marginalized
       communities—DNTs, NTs, and SNTs—who have faced systemic exclusion since colonial
